newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy bourse fails to open due technical problems.
newsitem.headline: Italy bourse fails to open due technical problems.

text.p: Italy's stock exchange failed to open on Monday, due to serious technical problems, for the first time since the Milan bourse started its move towards screen-based share trading in 1991.

A spokesman for the bourse council said that the stock market had suffered from a serious breakdown of its hardware and software systems this morning. This came after a number of temporary breakdowns in trading throughout last week.
Dealers said that this was just another setback for the reputation of the Milan bourse and its attempts to take its place alongside the major European stock markets of London, Paris and Frankfurt.

International investors are already wary of investing in Italian stocks due to worries that market regulations are not tight enough, as a number of large Italian listed companies have hit major financial problems with shareholders often surprised to see the severity of the crisis.

Dealers said that investors have suffered as groups such as Ferruzzi Finanziaria (now renamed Compart) Montedison, Gemina, Banco di Napoli and most recently Olivetti have shocked their shareholders on the size of their financial problems.

The Milan bourse is trying to rectify its problems by taking onboard the Eurosim law on European cross border share trading and planning for the privatisation of the exchange, while the advent of newly-privatised stocks such as oil giant ENI and telecoms holding STET was hoped to broaden the market's appeal.

But some dealers pointed out that market regulations for companies listing on the bourse need to be tighter and the reporting of financial details needs to be clearer to encourage more foreign investors to the Italian stock market.
The Milan bourse completed its move to screen trading in 1994.
